'''James Ray''' was a Decipher-era [[Squadron Members|Squadron Member]], listed as Gold 76 from Mentor, Oh. The published fan table marks the slot Retired after Decipher's SWCCG run.

Born in 1950, he holds a PhD in Chemistry from Cornell. He became a tournament director in mid-1997 and joined the squadron months later, ran family-supported tournaments east of Cleveland, and helped [[Ryan Patterson]] start out.<ref name="decsq-prof" />

== In their own words ==

<blockquote>
I am most likely one of the older squadron members in age, coming into this
world in 1950.  I have a PhD in Chemistry from Cornell University, where I
met Kathy McCracken, who now writes for Decipher as Major Rakal(It's such a small world!!).
We currently live in Mentor, Ohio, a Cleveland suburb located to the city's east, on the southern shores of Lake Erie.

We, my wife Cheryl, and two boys, Anthony and Nathan, first enjoyed
Decipher's Star Trek CCG, before Star Wars CCG was introduced.  Finally, the
temptation was overwhelming and that first Star Wars CCG starter deck was purchased.
The males of our family quickly migrated to the Star Wars CCG universe, but
Cheryl, bless her heart, still provides a tremendous amount of assistance
during our Star Wars CCG tournaments, for which I am truly grateful.

It has almost become a family Christmas tradition to buy a few boxes of either the latest
Star Wars or Star Trek (yes, we still collect them too) CCG boosters as a
family present, divide the commons/uncommons evenly, then spread the rares
over the dining room table and draft with great excitement.

My road to becoming a squadron member is a common one traveled by many
others.  Despite frequent trips to Decipher's web site a few years ago, no
local sanctioned Star Wars CCG tournaments could be found, and we were traveling 2-3
hours to play. I became a sanctioned tournament director in mid-1997 in the
hopes of recruiting more local sanctioned TDs,  and joined the squadron ranks
a few months later.  Fortunately, there are now several sanctioned Star Wars CCG TDs
and an additional Squadron member (Ryan Patterson) in the area, though I
can't take credit for the increase. Our next goal is to have a local
representative at a Star Wars CCG world championship in the near future, and we are
working on the means to accomplish the goal. Certainly, one of the means is
to foster a robust, vibrant environment that mentors the beginners and
challenges the veterans.

Take care one and all. And, of course, May The Force Be With You, Always.<ref name="decsq-prof" />
</blockquote>

Decipher recruited volunteer Squadron Members in the 1990s to promote SWCCG locally (tournaments, demos, player support). "FL" is printed on some slots in the surviving tables.
